basis: Intellectual disability and developmental impairment define the disorder; other organ findings are below 30%.
Antibody-mediated encephalitis affects central and peripheral nervous systems; associated malignancies are separate diseases.
Intellectual disability and precocious puberty define the syndrome; obesity was reported in carrier mothers.
Ovarian germ-cell tumor arises in a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement is established.
Cardiac defects, scoliosis and ID define phenotype; strabismus 60%; esophageal anomalies 40% omitted at cap; melanoma annotation is not an established syndrome feature.
Immune dysregulation; alveolar hemorrhage/respiratory failure, endocrine autoimmunity and marrow hypocellularity each 1/1; arthritis 1/1 omitted at cap. Single-patient evidence.
Defined as a learning disability arising from neurological impairment of reading.
Placental trophoblastic disorder lies outside the axes; bleeding-related anemia is secondary, and hyperthyroidism occurs in only 5-29%.
Lysosomal lipid storage causes hepatic failure and intestinal malabsorption in 80-99%; anemia in 30-79% with reticuloendothelial disease. Developmental delay is secondary.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory insufficiency defines disease; renal, hepatic and retinal disease are variable and not established at >=30%.
Cobalamin processing defect; developmental delay and anemia/neutropenia each 2/2; structural heart defects and pulmonary hypertension 1/2. Evidence comes from very small cohorts.
Glomus-body neoplasm usually occupies dermis or subcutis of distal extremities, especially subungual tissue; visceral sites are uncommon.
Congenital cardiac and great-vessel malformations dominate; midline liver and polysplenia do not establish hepatic or hematologic dysfunction.
Histologic variant of a carcinoma arising in the kidney; metastatic risks do not qualify as organ involvement.
Toxic exposure directly injures and inflames bronchioles; no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is specified.
Inherited skeletal myopathy with muscle weakness and joint contractures; motor delay reflects muscle disease rather than established neural injury.
Congenital underdevelopment of one lung directly defines the affected organ.
Intraepidermal cutaneous carcinoma presenting as a verrucous plaque.
Limb and skeletal malformations define syndrome; cognitive impairment and eyelid ptosis each occur in 30-79%; skin hyperextensibility alone lacks documented functional damage.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder; hearing loss and other extracardiac abnormalities belong to minority subtypes.
Primary breast carcinoma lies outside the axes; receptor status does not establish endocrine disease, and metastases are not defining involvement.
Inherited melanin biosynthesis disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular abnormalities; reduced visual acuity is reported in 9/9.
Right-heart and pulmonary-artery malformations define disease; diminished pulmonary blood flow and hypoxemia do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Neurological parasomnia involving loss of normal REM muscle atonia; later neurodegenerative disease is a separate diagnosis.
Germ-cell carcinoma arises in the testis as a reproductive organ; hormone production or metastatic risk alone does not establish another axis.
